entries.source: Schunk, Johann Peter: Codex diplomaticus exhibens chartas historiam medii aevi illustrantes
entries.german: Quinque Provisores HEINRICI III. Archiep. Mogunt. & ecclesie Mogunt. inventarium ciste telonii in Erenfels conficiunt. Nos NYCOLAUS de Lapide Can. ecclesie Moguntine & JOHANNES de Randecken miles, una cum honorabili viro Domino CUNONE de Valkinstein Scol. ecclesie Mog. nec non strenuis viris EBIRHARDO de Rosenberg & JOHANNE de Beldirsheim militibus Domini nostri Domini HEYNRICI Archiepiscopi Moguntini & sue Ecclesie Moguntine Provisores recognosci- ...mus, nos tam ex parte nostra quam nostrorum Compromissorum predictorum nomine & pro ipsis, una cum LUDOWICO de Ameneburg scriptore thelonii in Erinvels Cistam eiusdem thelonii die date presencium apperuiffe, & nos in ea septingentas & octoginta octo libras cum decem solidis hallensium numismatis sibi equivalentis invenisse. In cuius rei testimonium sigillum dicte nostre provisionis presentibus est appensum in crastino Kathedre bti Petri apli, anno Dni M. CCC. XLVII.
entries.english: The five Provisors of HEINRICH III, Archbishop of Mainz, & of the Church of Mainz, draw up an inventory of the toll chest in Erenfels. We, NYCOLAUS de Lapide, Canon of the church of Mainz, & JOHANNES de Randecken, knight, together with the honorable man Lord CUNONE de Valkinstein, Scholar of the church of Mainz, and also the strenuous men Eberhard von Rosenberg & JOHANNE de Beldirsheim, knights, Provisors of our Lord, Lord HEYNRICH, Archbishop of Mainz, & of his Church of Mainz, acknowledge... [that] we, as much on our own behalf as in the name of and for our aforementioned Compromisers, together with LUDOWICO de Ameneburg, scribe of the toll in Erinvels, have opened the Chest of the same toll on the day of the date of these presents, and that we have found in it seven hundred and eighty-eight pounds with ten Hallensian shillings in coins equivalent to it. In testimony of which matter, the seal of our said provision is appended to these presents on the morrow of the Chair of the blessed Apostle Peter, in the year of the Lord 1347.
